A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of delusions in target-directed reinforcement learning. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with Skipper and LEAP on SwordShieldMonster and RandDistShift, including estimation errors, delusional behavior frequencies, and generalization performance across 20 seeds.

after.justification: v5 retains original experimental results for both agents and environments in Section 5 and Appendix B, including diagnostic and task-performance curves across 20 seeds.

M1.justification: The generate and pertask strategies, mixture proportions, and separate generator/estimator training remain unchanged. The Skipper pruning procedures and LEAP adaptations in Appendix C are already present in v1; rewritten explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Skipper and LEAP on SwordShieldMonster and RandDistShift, including the same four OOD difficulty levels. No dataset, domain, task, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding plots retain the same comparator membership: Skipper compares F-F, F-E, F-P, F-G, and three hybrids; LEAP compares F-E with the three hybrids. Changes to citations and plot legends do not introduce additional evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The stated settings remain the same: 50 training tasks, 1.5 million interactions, four groups of 20 OOD evaluation tasks, and the retained initial-state procedures. Both appendices already specify LEAP's 8×8 SSM evaluation and CEM population of 512 over 10 iterations.

E4.justification: Both retain the same generator-strategy comparisons, E.1 error decompositions, distance-stratified estimation analyses, and difficulty-specific OOD tests. The new Figure 4 explains an existing pertask mechanism rather than adding an experimental analysis; diagnostic curve revisions are covered under E6.

E5.justification: v1 labels all Figure 3 intervals as 95% confidence intervals. v5 specifies 50% intervals for panels c and g to reduce overlap, retaining 95% elsewhere. Both report 20 seeds; this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Several LEAP diagnostic curves change, particularly the RDS delusional-plan ratios in v1 Figure 11b versus v5 Figure 12b. Corresponding aggregate OOD success curves remain unchanged. Figure 2b also changes the illustrated second-leg distance from D=1.1? to D=10. These are localized result revisions, not broad performance gains.

T1.justification: The MDP objective and mathematical relabeling definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v5's added convergence discussion does not introduce a mathematical derivation or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain identifying delusion types, diagnosing training-related causes, and mitigating them through generate, pertask, mixtures, and separate training distributions. v5 foregrounds autonomous and preemptive correction, but these aims and applicability beyond HER were already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: v5 more clearly distinguishes generator hallucinations from estimator delusions. Figure 2b now identifies only the first planned step as delusional, refining the G.2 example. Section 4.1 also adds an expectation of correct estimation conditional on convergent learning rules. Existing TD-learning and LEAP failure limitations remain.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes from an explicit published-repository link in v1 to submitted source code in v5. The first-page public code link remains, as do the substantive implementation details in Appendix C. This changes access instructions without establishing a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: v5 adds Liu et al. (2022) on safe RL under observational perturbations and removes Ada et al. (2024), Kahneman (2017), Parr and Russell (1997), and Shah et al. (2022). The principal positioning relative to HER, Skipper, and LEAP remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of Sections 2–4 are rewritten. Related work moves after experiments, empirical guidelines become a standalone numbered section, and generator/estimator headings are reframed around their roles. The header changes to PREPRINT and acknowledgements are removed.

P2.justification: v5 redraws Figure 1, revises Figure 2 annotations, and adds the explanatory pertask diagram as Figure 4. Plot legends, some axes, captions, and figure placement are refined throughout. The existing tables and experimental subplot arrangements are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves clarity through rewritten explanations, clearer generator/estimator distinctions, the corrected G.2 illustration in Figure 2b, and the new pertask diagram. These provide limited explanatory and consistency gains without expanding the method or experimental coverage. The 50% intervals in Figure 3c/g display less uncertainty than v1's stated 95% intervals, but the change is explicitly disclosed.
